meaning: A flat slab or bar of something, like chocolate; also a pill or a small computer
trick: TABLET = a little flat TABLE-top piece.
examples: I got a tablet of chocolate and returned to the window to eat it.
He bought a tablet of soap at the shop.

meaning: A popular newspaper with short stories, gossip and big pictures
trick: TABLOID = a TABLE of LOUD gossip.
examples: He name-dropped so much it felt like talking to a tabloid reporter.
The tabloid printed rumours about the actor.

meaning: Saying very little; not liking to talk
trick: TACIT = silent; TACITURN = always silent in TURN.
examples: Since Boxer's death, Benjamin was more morose and taciturn than ever.
My grandfather was a taciturn man who rarely smiled.

meaning: Fixed in place with small pins or nails; also added on loosely
trick: TACKED = stuck up with a TACK (thumb pin).
examples: A coloured poster had been tacked to the wall.
She tacked a note to the door.

meaning: A planned way of doing something to get a result
trick: TACTIC = a TACT-ful trick to win.
examples: Laila tried a more lighthearted tactic.
Ignoring the bully was a good tactic.

meaning: Related to planning actions carefully to reach a goal
trick: TACTICAL = about TACTICS.
examples: A tactical review is the final and most vital piece of any review.
The coach made a tactical change at half-time.

meaning: (informal) A small amount; slightly
trick: TAD = a TAD is a TADpole-sized bit.
examples: In the mornings, he stooped just a tad.
The soup is a tad salty.

meaning: (... along) went with someone, following them; also labelled
trick: TAGGED along = stuck to you like a TAG.
examples: He ran up to me and tagged along.
My little brother tagged along to the movies.

meaning: To follow someone closely, often secretly
trick: TAIL someone = stick behind them like a TAIL.
examples: Laila would have to tail him home, helpless and trembling with resentment.
The detective was told to tail the suspect.

meaning: Followed closely behind someone
trick: TAILED = came behind, like a TAIL.
examples: The village leader came by once a month, tailed by a servant who carried a chicken.
The car was tailed by two police bikes.

meaning: A person who makes or alters clothes to fit
trick: TAILOR = cuts cloth to fit, even round your TAIL.
examples: Her father had promised her to a tailor some thirty years older than her.
I took my new trousers to the tailor to shorten them.

meaning: A soft, fine, sweet-smelling powder used on the skin
trick: TALCUM = TALC + UM: soft powder.
examples: Laila smelled soap and talcum, ammonia and urine.
She dusted the baby with talcum after the bath.

meaning: A story, often a personal or made-up one
trick: TALE = what you TELL.
examples: I never stopped long enough to appreciate the tale I told.
Grandma told us a tale about a clever fox.

usage.pattern: tell a tale / a tale of something

meaning: Counted or added up a total
trick: TALLIED = made TALLY marks to count.
examples: It was as though some accountant up there tallied things up.
The teacher tallied the votes on the board.

meaning: Shrubs or small trees with thin feathery leaves that grow in dry, salty places
trick: TAMARISKS = TAMe shrubs that RISK the desert.
examples: Some of them were half hidden in clumps of tamarisks.
Tamarisks grew along the dry riverbed.

meaning: A long-necked Indian string instrument that plays a steady background drone
trick: TAMBOURA = TANPURA, the steady hum behind a singer.
examples: Laila hears music at Kabul's street corners: tabla, harmonium and tamboura.
The singer tuned the tamboura before the concert.

meaning: (Of an animal) used to people, not wild; also dull
trick: TAME = TAMEd by a TAMEr in the circus.
examples: The pigs had to counteract the lies put about by Moses, the tame raven.
The deer in the park are so tame they eat from your hand.

meaning: (in ...) together, at the same time; also one behind the other
trick: TANDEM bicycle = two riders working together.
examples: Then Marie proposed that we should swim tandem.
The two teams worked in tandem to finish on time.

usage.pattern: do something (in) tandem / in tandem with someone

meaning: A large clay oven used for baking bread and cooking meat
trick: TANDOOR = TANDOORi roti comes from here.
examples: Once she had floured the dough, she set out for the communal tandoor.
The naan comes straight out of the hot tandoor.

meaning: A strong, sharp taste or smell
trick: TANG = TANGy like lemon on your TONGue.
examples: A morning breeze was blowing and it had a pleasant salty tang.
This yogurt has a nice lemony tang.

usage.pattern: a + adjective + tang / the tang of something

meaning: Moving away from the main subject; only slightly related
trick: TANGENTIAL = going off on a TANGENT.
examples: She was tangential with her topics, and her hands moved wildly.
His answer was tangential to the question I asked.

meaning: Real and able to be seen, touched or measured
trick: TANGIBLE = you can TANG (touch) it, from Latin tangere = touch.
examples: Bad values involve tangible external goals outside of our control.
We need tangible results, not promises.

meaning: A twisted, mixed-up mass of things
trick: TANGLE = like TANGLEd hair or wires.
examples: Mariam and Aziza were a tangle of limbs, rolling and giggling.
The cat played with a tangle of wool.

meaning: In a way that makes you want something you cannot quite have
trick: From King TANTALUS, who stood in water and under fruit he could never reach.
examples: He dangled before her, tantalizingly, what would make her happiest, then pulled it away.
The cake sat tantalizingly on the shelf, just out of reach.

usage.pattern: tantalizingly + close/near / be tantalizingly out of reach

meaning: Almost the same as, or as bad as, something else
trick: TANTAMOUNT = 'that amount' - the same amount as something else.
examples: Throwing out my Metallica shirts was tantamount to a death sentence for a teenager in 1998.
Not replying to her message is tantamount to saying no.

usage.pattern: be tantamount to something / to doing something

meaning: A sudden fit of anger and shouting, often childish
trick: TANTRUM - a child throws a TANTRUM, banging on a drum.
examples: People with strong boundaries are not afraid of a temper tantrum or an argument.
The little boy threw a tantrum in the toy shop.

meaning: Followers of Taoism, a Chinese way of life that teaches living simply and in harmony with nature
trick: TAO = 'the Way'; TAOISTS follow the Way (say 'DOW-ists').
examples: Like the Taoists say, those who know don't speak, and those who speak don't know.
Ancient Taoists believed in living in harmony with nature.

meaning: Heavy cloths with pictures or patterns woven into them, hung on walls
trick: TAPESTRIES - like TAPE stretched across walls, but woven with pictures.
examples: She saw the frayed ends of richly colored tapestries hanging from the walls.
The old castle walls were covered with beautiful tapestries.

meaning: A room in a pub or inn where drinks are served
trick: A TAP pours beer; the TAPROOM is the room with the taps.
examples: Jones spent his days in the taproom of the Red Lion, complaining to anyone who would listen.
They met for a drink in the hotel taproom.

usage.pattern: in/at the taproom of a place

meaning: The hard black surface of a runway or road; also an airport runway area
trick: TARMAC = TAR + MACadam (road made of tar and stones).
examples: A pick-up truck came bouncing down the tarmac in our direction.
The plane waited on the tarmac for an hour before take-off.

usage.pattern: on the tarmac / down the tarmac

meaning: (Of metal or glass) dull and no longer shiny; also (of a reputation) damaged
trick: TARNISHED - its shine has TURNED to dust.
examples: The room had a wardrobe with a tarnished mirror.
Grandma polished the tarnished silver spoons until they shone.

usage.pattern: a tarnished + mirror/reputation / be tarnished by something

meaning: A set of special picture cards used to try to tell the future
hindi: टैरो पत्ते, भविष्य बताने के पत्ते
trick: TAROT rhymes with 'carrot' - pick a card and see your future.
examples: She started believing in energy healing, angels and tarot cards.
My aunt reads tarot cards for her friends.

usage.pattern: read tarot cards / a tarot + reading/card

meaning: A large heavy waterproof sheet used to cover things
trick: TARPAULIN gives us the Hindi word 'तिरपाल'.
examples: For the time being, the floor is covered with tarpaulin.
We put a tarpaulin over the bikes to keep off the rain.

meaning: Covered with tar, a thick black sticky substance
trick: TARRED = TAR + RED; fresh TAR on the road.
examples: Presently we struck a patch of freshly tarred road.
The workers tarred the roof to stop the leaks.

meaning: Torn rags or strips; also a ruined state (in ...)
trick: TATTERS - TORN + SCATTERS: torn bits scattered.
examples: She feared their life together would soon come loose again in strips and tatters.
After the storm, the flag hung in tatters.

meaning: A person, usually a child, who tells others' secrets or reports bad behaviour (informal)
trick: TATTLE = chatter; a TATTLETALE tattles TALES to the teacher.
examples: He sensed now that his tattletale game had let something serious into the room.
Don't be a tattletale - let them sort it out themselves.

usage.pattern: be a tattletale / call someone a tattletale

meaning: Making fun of someone or provoking them in a cruel way
trick: TAUNTING - like an AUNT who keeps TEASING you.
examples: It was God's fault, for taunting her as He had.
The older boys kept taunting him about his glasses.

meaning: Pulled or stretched tight; also tense and anxious
trick: TAUT sounds like 'TAUGHT' - a TIGHT rope that's been taught to stay stiff.
examples: My body was taut with tension and throbbing with pain.
Pull the rope taut before you tie the knot.

usage.pattern: be taut (with something) / pull something taut

meaning: Of a warm orange-brown colour with a red tint
trick: TAWNY = colour of a lion's coat; TAWNY-RED = lion colour with red.
examples: The tawny-red earth pattered on Mother's coffin.
The fox had a bushy tawny-red tail.

meaning: A cup from which tea is drunk
trick: TEA + CUP = TEACUP.
examples: He slowly turns his teacup on its saucer, one way, then the other.
She poured milk into her teacup.

meaning: A kettle used for boiling water for tea
trick: TEA + KETTLE = TEAKETTLE.
examples: On the shelves sat clay pots and pans, a blackened teakettle, cups and spoons.
The teakettle whistled on the stove.

meaning: The state of being boring and repetitive
trick: TEDIUM - TEDIOUS work leads to TEDIUM.
examples: The media never show us the thousands of hours of dull practice and tedium behind success.
Music helped him get through the tedium of the long drive.

usage.pattern: the tedium of something / relieve the tedium

meaning: Set herself up for something, made it likely (... up, informal); also placed a golf ball on its peg
trick: TEED up - like a golf ball placed on a TEE, ready to be hit.
examples: Other times she knew she teed herself up for a beating.
He teed up the ball and swung his club.

meaning: To move unsteadily from side to side, about to fall; (...-totter) a seesaw
trick: TEETER-TOTTER - a seesaw that goes up and down, never steady.
examples: I saw six boats teeter tottering in and out of view on the waves.
The vase began to teeter on the edge of the table.

usage.pattern: teeter on the edge/brink of something

meaning: Moved unsteadily, as if about to fall
trick: TEETERED - wobbled like a toddler on its TEE-tiny feet.
examples: When I teetered toward her, I saw her in triplicate.
The tired runner teetered across the finish line.

meaning: A small spinning top; (like a ...) turning round and round
trick: TEETOTUM - a TOT's TOy that spins.
examples: He was turning like a teetotum, looking in all directions.
The child spun the little teetotum on the table.

meaning: Sending thoughts or feelings to another mind without speaking
trick: TELE = far + PATHY = feeling: feeling from far away.
examples: Think of it as a kind of involuntary telepathy between people.
The twins joked that they had telepathy.

meaning: A person's usual nature, especially how they react and feel
trick: TEMPERAMENT - your TEMPER is part of your TEMPERAMENT.
examples: She lived in fear of his shifting moods and volatile temperament.
My brother has a calm temperament.

usage.pattern: someone's temperament / have a calm/fiery temperament

meaning: A strong wish to do something, especially something you shouldn't
trick: TEMPTATION - TEMPT + ACTION: the urge to act.
examples: For weeks, the temptation to pull back had been ever present.
I resisted the temptation to eat another cookie.

usage.pattern: the temptation to do something / resist temptation

meaning: To look after someone or something (... to); also to usually do something
trick: TEND = aTTEND to someone.
examples: You should tend to your son now.
She tends her garden every morning.

usage.pattern: tend (to) someone/something / tend to do something

meaning: Looked after someone or something
trick: TENDED = aTTENDED to.
examples: She had been tended to by a doctor at a hospital in Herat.
The nurse tended the wounded soldier.

usage.pattern: tend (to) someone / be tended by someone

meaning: Painful when touched; also gentle and loving, or (of food) soft
trick: TENDER - a TENDER spot hurts; a TENDER heart is soft.
examples: The shin was tender to the touch.
My arm is still tender where I got the injection.

meaning: To make meat soft; (figuratively) to wear someone down with hard treatment
trick: TENDERIZE = make TENDER, like beating meat soft.
examples: Those first weeks tenderize new recruits until only the strongest are left.
Soak the meat in yogurt to tenderize it.

meaning: Gentle, loving kindness; also soreness when touched
trick: TENDERNESS - a TENDER heart is full of TENDERNESS.
examples: Laila caught a glimpse of the tenderness that had once bound her parents.
She spoke to the child with great tenderness.

meaning: A strong cord in the body that joins a muscle to a bone
trick: TENDON - it TENDS (stretches) between muscle and bone.
examples: Each time my medial tendon twinged, it felt like a raw nerve.
He hurt a tendon in his heel while playing football.

meaning: Strong cords in the body that join muscles to bones
trick: TENDONS - they TEND (stretch) between muscle and bone.
examples: My medial tendons were wobbly and I still had stress fractures.
Stretching before a run protects your tendons.

meaning: Thin curling strands of something like smoke or hair; also curling stems of climbing plants
trick: TENDRILS - TENDER little curls that twist like a DRILL.
examples: Kabul was silent, quilted in white, tendrils of smoke snaking up here and there.
Tendrils of her hair escaped from her ponytail.

meaning: A main belief or principle of a theory or group
trick: TENET - TEN commandments are each a TENET.
examples: Its first and central tenet was that pain and loss are inevitable.
Honesty is a basic tenet of our family.

meaning: Full of worry and nervous strain
trick: TENSE - TENSION makes things TENSE.
examples: I'd never experienced a hostage situation so tense, so personal.
The last minutes of the match were very tense.

meaning: Not certain or confident; done carefully and without sureness
trick: TENTATIVE - like testing a TENT before you trust it.
examples: Mariam slowly grew used to this tentative but pleasant companionship.
He gave a tentative smile.

usage.pattern: a tentative + step/smile / be tentative about something

meaning: In a hesitant, unsure way
trick: TENTATIVELY - stepping carefully, like into a dark TENT.
examples: Tariq's fingers tentatively began to slip into hers.
She tentatively raised her hand to ask a question.

meaning: Only slightly warm; also not enthusiastic
trick: TEPID - TEPID water is TEPID: neither hot nor cold (think 'tap is tepid').
examples: The sun wasn't too hot, but the water was pleasantly tepid.
He didn't like drinking tepid tea.

meaning: An area of land, especially its physical features
trick: TERRAIN - TERRA means earth.
examples: Gary had done the race before and knew the terrain.
Our car struggled on the rocky terrain.

usage.pattern: know the terrain / over rough terrain

meaning: An area of land that someone controls or claims
trick: TERRITORY - TERRA = land; land that is yours.
examples: The kites were now timid trespassers in territory claimed by rockets and jets.
The cat defends its territory from other cats.

meaning: Clear proof or evidence of something; also (Old/New ...) part of the Bible
trick: A TESTAMENT TESTifies to something.
examples: The novel is a sad and beautiful testament to Afghan suffering and strength.
Her success is a testament to her hard work.

usage.pattern: be a testament to something / bear testament to something

meaning: To give evidence in a court of law
trick: TESTIFY - a witness TESTS the truth in court.
examples: I want to see you before I testify.
She agreed to testify against the thief.

meaning: A formal statement of what someone saw, given in a court
trick: TESTIMONY - what you say when you TESTIFY.
examples: Eyewitness testimony isn't always taken seriously in court cases.
His testimony helped the jury decide.

meaning: Tied to something with a rope so it cannot move far
trick: TETHERED - TIED with a TETHER (rope).
examples: Laila watched three men talking near a cow tethered to a fence.
The goat was tethered to a post in the field.

meaning: Exaggerated and showy, as if acting; also to do with the theatre
trick: THEATRICAL - acting like you're in a THEATRE.
examples: Someone periodically let out a theatrical, sorrow-drenched sob.
He gave a theatrical sigh and rolled his eyes.

meaning: To do with the study of God and religious beliefs
trick: THEO = God + LOGICAL = the logic of God.
examples: The Buddha argued this from a theological and philosophical perspective.
They had a long theological debate about faith.

usage.pattern: from a theological perspective / theological + noun

meaning: Helping to heal or to make someone feel better
trick: THERAPEUTIC - like THERAPY, it heals.
examples: The FBI experimented with new and old therapeutic techniques.
Gardening can be very therapeutic.

meaning: A thick group of bushes or small trees growing close together
trick: THICKET - a THICK patch of bushes.
examples: There is a pomegranate tree in the yard and a thicket of sweetbriar bushes.
The rabbit hid in a thicket.

meaning: Thick groups of bushes or small trees growing close together
trick: THICKETS - THICK patches of bushes.
examples: We pushed through tall grass and around thickets of shrubs.
Birds nest in the thickets by the river.

meaning: In a voice that is low and not clear, often from emotion; also in a thick layer
hindi: भारी आवाज़ में; मोटी परत में
trick: THICKLY - words come out THICK when you're about to cry.
examples: "Can you do that?" she said thickly.
He spread the butter thickly on his toast.

usage.pattern: say something thickly / spread something thickly

meaning: Stealing things; dishonest
trick: THIEVING - what a THIEF does.
examples: Everything was done for themselves, not for a pack of idle, thieving human beings.
The thieving monkeys grabbed our bananas.

meaning: A small cap worn on a finger when sewing; also a very small amount
trick: THIMBLE - a tiny cap for your THUMB (well, finger).
examples: I ate a chicken breast and some vegetables along with a thimble of rice.
Grandma wore a silver thimble while she sewed.

usage.pattern: a thimble of something / wear a thimble

meaning: The feeling of needing something to drink; also a strong desire
trick: THIRST - dry as the FIRST day of summer.
examples: Finally, it was thirst that pulled her out of bed.
He drank three glasses of water to quench his thirst.

usage.pattern: quench someone's thirst / a thirst for something

meaning: A wild plant with prickly leaves and purple flowers
trick: THISTLE - THIS'LL prick you!
examples: She watched a caterpillar inching along the foot of a young thistle.
The thistle is the national flower of Scotland.

meaning: A main road through a town or city
trick: THOROUGHFARE - a road you go THROUGH and pay the FARE.
examples: Spectators had gathered on both sides of the thoroughfare.
The market is on a busy thoroughfare.

meaning: Quiet and thinking deeply; also kind and caring about others
trick: THOUGHTFUL = full of THOUGHTS.
examples: His face was more thoughtful, more solemn, than his younger brother's.
Thank you for the flowers - that was very thoughtful.

usage.pattern: a thoughtful + face/look / it's thoughtful of someone to do

meaning: Hit or tossed something violently and repeatedly; also beat badly in a game
trick: THRASHED - like the waves CRASHED and SMASHED.
examples: Cold water swiped the breath from our lungs as the waves thrashed us.
Our team got thrashed 5-0 last night.

usage.pattern: thrash someone/something / be thrashed by someone

meaning: Moving or tossing about violently
trick: THRASHING - waves CRASHING and THRASHING.
examples: I couldn't see the boats out past the thrashing waves.
The fish was thrashing about in the net.

meaning: (Of a voice) thin and weak; also (of cloth) worn thin from use
trick: THREADBARE - cloth so worn you can see the BARE THREADS.
examples: Then Jalil spoke, in a thin, threadbare voice.
He wore a threadbare old coat.

meaning: Moving carefully through a crowd or narrow space
trick: THREADING - like a THREAD going through the eye of a needle.
examples: The cars crawled up the street, threading through the hawkers and pedestrians.
The waiter was threading his way between the tables.

meaning: (Of corn or wheat) beaten to separate the grain from the stalks
trick: THRESHED - the grain is THRASHED out of the stalk.
examples: The corn was cut and stacked and some of it was already threshed.
The farmers threshed the wheat after the harvest.

meaning: Beating corn or wheat to separate the grain from the stalks
trick: THRESHING - THRASHING the wheat to free the grain.
examples: Electricity could operate threshing machines, ploughs and reapers.
The village bought a new threshing machine.

meaning: Grew strong or did very well; (thrive on/off) enjoyed and grew stronger because of
trick: THRIVED - THREE-VED: did three times better.
examples: I thrived off the beauty of seeing a man broken, only to rise again.
The plants thrived in the sunny window.

usage.pattern: thrive on/off something / thrive in a place

meaning: A strong regular beat, as of pain or the heart
trick: THROB - like a THROBBING heart: thump, thump.
examples: With each throb my hate spiked.
She felt a dull throb in her head.

meaning: Beat with steady pulses of pain
trick: THROBBED - pain went thump, thump, thump.
examples: My quads throbbed and my feet were chafed and bleeding.
His thumb throbbed after he hit it with the hammer.

meaning: Beating with steady pulses, usually of pain; also humming with sound
trick: THROBBING - a THROBBING head goes thump, thump.
examples: My temples were throbbing and I could hardly drag myself along.
I woke up with a throbbing headache.

meaning: Squeezing someone's throat so they can't breathe
trick: THROTTLING - grabbing the THROAT.
examples: Her body shook as if something were throttling her from the inside.
The tight collar felt like it was throttling him.

meaning: Made a low steady humming or vibrating sound or feeling
trick: THRUMMED - like fingers DRUMMING a low hum.
examples: That potent cocktail of fear and rage thrummed through my veins.
The engine thrummed beneath our feet.

meaning: Making a low steady beating or humming sound
trick: THRUMMING - DRUMMING with a low hum.
examples: My heart was thrumming like Morse code.
We could hear the rain thrumming on the roof.

meaning: Forced on someone (... upon); also pushed suddenly and hard
trick: THRUST - like a sudden push into the TRUST circle you didn't ask for.
examples: It feels like a problem that was somehow thrust upon you without your choosing.
She thrust the letter into my hand and left.

usage.pattern: thrust something upon someone / thrust something into something

meaning: Making a dull heavy beating sound
trick: THUDDING - THUD, THUD, THUD.
examples: She became aware of the blood thudding in her ears.
I heard footsteps thudding up the stairs.

meaning: A rough, violent person, often a criminal; (informal) a tough, fearless person
trick: THUG - from Hindi 'ठग' (cheat, robber).
examples: She was grumpy and took no nonsense, and I loved that thug in her.
The thug grabbed her bag and ran.

meaning: A dull heavy sound of something hitting; also a hard hit
trick: THUMP - THUD + BUMP.
examples: The belt made a thump when he dropped it to the ground.
The book fell to the floor with a thump.

usage.pattern: with a thump / give someone a thump

meaning: Beating hard and loudly
trick: THUMPING - THUMP, THUMP, like a drum.
examples: She became intensely aware of her heart thumping.
My heart was thumping before the exam.

meaning: Stopped someone from doing what they planned
trick: THWARTED - a WART that blocked the plan.
examples: The investigation thwarted a plot to set off bombs in New York.
Heavy rain thwarted our plans for a picnic.

usage.pattern: thwart something / be thwarted by something

meaning: The front and larger of the two bones in the lower leg
trick: TIBIA - Latin for 'flute'; it's long and straight like one.
examples: Each turn of the ankle felt like venom flowing through the marrow of my tibia.
She broke her tibia when she fell skiing.

meaning: Relating to the rise and fall of the sea; (... wave) a huge wave, or a huge amount of something
trick: TIDAL - TIDE + AL.
examples: There's no way we can process the tidal waves of information flowing past us.
Their party won by a tidal wave of votes.

meaning: The general direction in which things are moving (the ... turns); also the rise and fall of the sea
trick: TIDE - when the TIDE turns, the ocean changes direction.
examples: In the closing months of 1944, the tide was turning against Japan.
The tide comes in twice a day.

meaning: Made neat and clean
trick: TIDIED - made TIDY.
examples: The keeper took me to his room, and I tidied myself up a bit.
She tidied her desk before going home.

meaning: News or information (old-fashioned)
trick: TIDINGS - news that comes in like the TIDE.
examples: Hearken to my joyful tidings of the golden future time.
The messenger brought glad tidings to the king.

meaning: (Of money) large (a ... sum, informal); also neat and in order
trick: A TIDY sum - a neat, big pile of money.
examples: I was keeping her, as a matter of fact, and she cost me a tidy sum.
He made a tidy profit from selling his old car.

meaning: Prepares and works land for growing crops; also (as a noun) cash drawers in a shop
hindi: जोतता है, खेती करता है; गल्ला
trick: TILLS the soil TILL the crops grow.
examples: Our labour tills the soil, yet not one of us owns more than his bare skin.
The farmer tills his field every spring.

meaning: Moved or leaned so that one side is higher than the other
trick: TILT = TIP a little; TILTED = tipped to one side.
examples: The springs creaked as the bed tilted to his side.
She tilted her head and smiled at me.

usage.pattern: something tilted (to one side) / tilted something up/forward

meaning: A moment felt so intense or important that it seemed to stop
trick: Like a paused video: the clock stops ticking in that moment.
examples: Time stood still as I realized I had always looked at my life from the wrong perspective.
When I saw the exam result, time stood still.

partners: time stood still for a moment

meaning: Lacking courage or confidence; easily frightened
trick: TIMID sounds like 'tum mid' — hides in the middle of the crowd.
examples: With snow came the kites, now timid trespassers in skies claimed by rockets and jets.
The timid puppy hid behind the sofa.

meaning: A small amount of a colour, feeling or quality
trick: TINGE = a TINy touch of something.
examples: When he spoke, it was with a tinge of guile and tenderness.
There was a tinge of sadness in her voice.

meaning: A light, clear, ringing sound, like a small bell or running water
trick: TINKLE sounds like tiny bells: tin-tin-tinkle.
examples: It was all sunlight and silence except for the tinkle of the stream.
I heard the tinkle of glasses in the kitchen.

meaning: A slight shade or trace of a colour
trick: TINT = a TINy bit of colour.
examples: Her hair had an odd purple tint to it.
The car windows have a dark tint.

usage.pattern: a + colour + tint / have a tint to it

meaning: The pointed or rounded ends of something; also small extra payments for service
trick: Finger TIPS are at the very top, the TIPpy end.
examples: His nails were yellow-brown, and some of the tips were curling.
The tips of my fingers were cold.

meaning: Long, angry speeches criticising someone or something
trick: TIRADES make you TIRED — they go on and on with RAGE.
examples: The only things that caught my attention were his gestures and some elaborate tirades.
He went on angry tirades about the traffic every morning.

meaning: Working very hard without seeming to get tired
trick: TIRE-LESS = no tiredness at all.
examples: We thank David Grossman, Helen Heller, and the tireless Chandler Crawford.
Our tireless teacher stayed late to help every student.

meaning: Laughed quietly in a nervous or silly way
trick: TITTER sounds like TEE-hee-hee — a small nervous laugh.
examples: At this some people tittered, and my lawyer spoke sternly.
The children tittered when the teacher dropped her book.

meaning: Laughing quietly in a nervous or silly way
trick: TITTER sounds like TEE-hee-hee — a small nervous laugh.
examples: It sounded nonsensical, and I heard people tittering.
The girls kept tittering at the back of the class.

meaning: Short, quiet, nervous or silly laughs
trick: TITTERS = little TEE-hee laughs.
examples: There were some titters in court.
His mistake drew a few titters from the audience.

usage.pattern: titters from someone / a few titters

meaning: Exactly or perfectly, in every detail
trick: TO A T: as exact as a T-square ruler.
examples: Erin follows all the lessons she's learned to a T.
The new dress fits her to a T.

meaning: A person or shop that sells cigarettes, cigars and tobacco
trick: TOBACCO + -NIST = the one who sells tobacco (like a florIST sells flowers).
examples: The tobacconist across the street brought a chair out on to the pavement.
He bought a newspaper at the tobacconist on the corner.

meaning: The hard flat covers on the tips of the toes
trick: TOE + NAILS = nails on your toes.
examples: My white socks were stained from cracked toenails and broken blisters.
Please cut your toenails before wearing new shoes.

meaning: Worked very hard for a long time, usually at tiring physical work
trick: TOILED = TOILing like a farmer under the sun; 'toil and trouble'.
examples: The animals toiled harder than ever, carrying blocks of stone all day.
My grandfather toiled in the fields all his life.

meaning: Working very hard, or moving slowly and with great effort
hindi: कड़ी मेहनत करते हुए, जूझते हुए
trick: TOILING = toil + ing — sweating and struggling.
examples: To see him toiling up the slope inch by inch filled everyone with admiration.
The workers were toiling in the hot sun.

meaning: Done only for show, small and not serious; also (as a noun) a sign or symbol of something
trick: A TOKEN effort is like a TOKEN coin — small and not the real thing.
examples: Sometimes he'd put in some token effort, but nothing ever happened.
He paid only a token amount for the old bike.

meaning: Able to be accepted or put up with; also fairly good
trick: TOLERABLE = ABLE to TOLERATE it.
examples: It still hurt to walk, but the pain was more tolerable.
The heat was tolerable in the evening.

meaning: Willing to accept or put up with others' behaviour or views, sometimes with quiet patience
trick: TOLERANT people TOLERATE others.
examples: Mariam took in their plucked eyebrows and the thin, tolerant smiles they gave her.
My grandmother is very tolerant of our noise.

meaning: Rang a large bell slowly and repeatedly
trick: TOLLED = the bell TOLD everyone with its slow ring.
examples: To our right was the bell that 130 classmates tolled in order to quit training.
The church bell tolled at noon.

usage.pattern: someone tolled a bell / a bell tolled

meaning: A stone over a grave showing the name of the dead person
trick: TOMB + STONE = the stone on a tomb.
examples: On Bukowski's tombstone, the epitaph reads: "Don't try."
We read the old names on each tombstone.

meaning: Not understanding what others feel or want; also unable to hear differences in musical notes
hindi: असंवेदनशील, नासमझ; सुर न पहचानने वाला
trick: TONE-DEAF = deaf to the 'tone' of the room, not just of music.
examples: Onoda tried to espouse the values of Old Japan, but he was tone-deaf to this new society.
The company's tone-deaf advert upset many people.

usage.pattern: be tone-deaf to something / a tone-deaf + remark/response

meaning: A small hut in a garden where tools are kept
trick: TOOL + SHED = a little shed full of tools.
examples: Near the well was a tool-shed, and a bicycle leaning against the wall.
Dad keeps the lawnmower in the tool-shed.

meaning: A short, high sound from a horn, whistle or flute
trick: TOOT-TOOT says the horn — the word is the sound.
examples: They awoke to the high-pitched toot of a flute from the hillside.
The driver gave a quick toot of the horn.

meaning: Showing the shape and height of the land, such as hills and valleys
trick: TOPO (place) + GRAPHIC (drawing) = a drawing of a place's shape.
examples: We learned to judge distance and how to draw our own topographic maps.
Hikers carry a topographic map to find the trail.

meaning: Foods served with or put on top of a main dish, like rice or pizza
hindi: ऊपर डाली चीज़ें, साथ की सब्ज़ियाँ
trick: TOPPINGS go on TOP of the dish.
examples: Nana taught her to cook rice and all the different toppings: stew, spinach, cauliflower.
I like extra cheese and olives as pizza toppings.

meaning: Made something fall over; also made someone lose power
hindi: गिरा दिया, उलट दिया; सत्ता से हटाया
trick: TOPPLED = the TOP fell over.
examples: If Zalmai toppled a rack of shoes, Rasheed scolded him gently.
The cat toppled a vase off the table.

usage.pattern: someone toppled something / something toppled over

meaning: Falling over; also losing power or being defeated
trick: TOPPLING = TOP-heavy and falling.
examples: The territories they had won were now toppling like dominoes to U.S. forces.
The tall stack of books was toppling over.

usage.pattern: something is toppling (over) / toppling like dominoes

meaning: Made to suffer badly, often by being bullied or teased again and again
trick: TORMENT = TORture of the MENTal kind.
examples: I was born broken and was tormented in school.
The new boy was tormented by older kids.

meaning: People who make someone suffer by hurting or bullying them
trick: TORMENT + ORS = the ones who torment.
examples: With one accord, they flung themselves upon their tormentors.
She finally stood up to her tormentors.

meaning: Spoiled or destroyed a plan or chance; also hit a ship with a torpedo
trick: A TORPEDO sinks ships; TORPEDOED sinks plans.
examples: When I met a woman I liked, my self-absorption quickly torpedoed everything.
The rain torpedoed our picnic plans.

meaning: Twisted something with force so it turns
trick: TORQUE = twisting force (like a spanner); TORQUED = twisted hard.
examples: I torqued my hips to keep my legs moving.
He torqued the bolt tight with a spanner.

meaning: Full of twists and turns; also long and complicated
trick: TORTUOUS twists like a TORTOISE path; don't confuse with TORTUROUS (painful).
examples: Laila remembered Tariq's strong hands with the tortuous, full veins on their backs.
We drove up a tortuous mountain road.

meaning: A sacred symbol of a group; in '... pole', a ranking of people from top to bottom
trick: A TOTEM pole stacks faces from TOP to bottom — like a ranking.
examples: For years he lived as a bum, at the bottom of the social totem pole.
As the new intern, I was low on the totem pole.

usage.pattern: low on the totem pole / a totem of something

meaning: Walked or moved unsteadily, as if about to fall
trick: TOTTERED like a TOT (toddler) learning to walk.
examples: Aziza tottered from Laila to Mariam, then back.
The old man tottered across the room.

meaning: Moving or walking unsteadily, as if about to fall
trick: TOTTERING like a TOT (toddler) taking first steps.
examples: The girl was tottering forward, one arm across her belly.
The tottering pile of plates finally fell.

meaning: Travel around a place, visiting several towns or sites, often for work or pleasure
trick: TOUR = go round and round (TOURists move 'round' places).
examples: He would teach at Harvard and tour much of the United States giving lectures.
The band will tour Europe next summer.

usage.pattern: tour + a place / go on tour

meaning: Made someone's hair untidy, often in a friendly way
trick: TOUSLED = TUSSLED hair — messed up as if in a playful tussle.
examples: He patted the heads of some and tousled their hair, without condescension.
Grandpa tousled my hair and laughed.

meaning: Pale yellow and rough-looking, like flax fibre (of hair); rare
trick: TOW = flax fibre; TOWY hair looks like TOW — think 'tow-headed'.
examples: His towy hair has gone very thin, and he has reddish blotches on his face.
The farm boy had towy hair that shone in the sun.

meaning: Easy to control, manage or train
trick: TRACTABLE = easy to TRACT (pull) along, like a TRACTOR pulling a cart.
examples: Bulls which had always been tractable suddenly turned savage.
The new puppy is calm and tractable.

meaning: Illegal buying and selling of things like drugs, weapons or people
trick: TRAFFIC of goods on a secret road = TRAFFICKING.
examples: Special forces help control problems like terrorism and drug trafficking.
Police arrested the gang for drug trafficking.

meaning: A rough path through countryside or forest; also marks left by someone moving
trick: A TRAIL is a path you TRAveL on foot.
examples: I wondered if the quarter mile I skipped on the road or trail would cost me.
We walked along a forest trail.

usage.pattern: on/along a trail / a + mountain/forest trail

meaning: Walking or going around from place to place, often tiredly or without clear purpose
trick: TRAIPSING = TRAmping + strolling about on endless trips.
examples: When I was young I was searching for the truth, traipsing about, calling on philosophers.
We spent all day traipsing around the shops.

meaning: The path or general direction in which something develops or moves
trick: TRAJECTORY = the TRAck an object or a life JECTs (throws) along.
examples: As guides for the overall trajectory of our life, they are useless.
Her career is on an upward trajectory.

usage.pattern: the trajectory of something / on a + upward/downward trajectory

meaning: An electric vehicle that runs on rails along city streets
trick: TRAM runs on TRAck rails through town (Kolkata has them).
examples: The jurymen reminded me of a row of passengers on one side of a tram.
We took a tram to the city centre.

usage.pattern: take/ride a tram / on a tram

meaning: Walk with heavy steps, often for a long way; also (as a noun) a homeless wanderer
trick: TRAMP sounds like stomping feet: tramp, tramp, tramp.
examples: Boxer and Clover would tramp steadily round and round the field.
We had to tramp through the snow to reach the village.

meaning: Walking a long way, or wandering around as a homeless traveller
trick: TRAMPING = living like a TRAMP, walking from town to town.
examples: Orwell was one of the names he had used while tramping round England.
They spent the summer tramping through the hills.

meaning: Stepped heavily on and crushed; also harmed or ignored something precious
trick: TRAMPLED = TRAMPed on until flat.
examples: To catch the grace of a new season before it was trampled and corrupted?
The flowers were trampled by the crowd.

meaning: A half-conscious, dreamy state in which someone seems unaware of what is around them
trick: TRANCE = TRANSported away in your mind.
examples: I went from four pull-ups to three, and found my trance again.
She stared at the sea as if in a trance.

usage.pattern: in a trance / fall into a trance

meaning: Like a dreamy, half-conscious state
trick: TRANCE + LIKE = like being in a trance.
examples: The therapist put the client into a trancelike state.
The music put him in a trancelike mood.

meaning: A state of peace and calm (British spelling; US 'tranquility')
trick: TRANQUILLITY = a TRANQUIL lake; double L for a double dose of calm.
examples: For Laila, life in Murree is one of comfort and tranquillity.
We enjoyed the tranquillity of the village.

usage.pattern: the tranquillity of something / peace and tranquillity

meaning: Rise above or go beyond a limit, difficulty or personal feeling
trick: TRANS (across) + SCEND (climb) = climb across and above.
examples: Love requires that you transcend your own personal preferences.
Good music can transcend language barriers.

meaning: Crossing or covering a whole continent
trick: TRANS (across) + CONTINENTAL = across the continent.
examples: This was in the 1860s, so transcontinental travel was difficult and dangerous.
They took a transcontinental train from coast to coast.

meaning: Pierced through with something sharp; also made unable to move from shock or wonder
trick: TRANS (through) + FIXED = fixed right through, or fixed to the spot.
examples: A shaft of light shot up, and I felt as if a long, thin blade transfixed my forehead.
The children stood transfixed by the magic show.

usage.pattern: something transfixed someone / be transfixed by something

meaning: Letting some light through but not completely clear
trick: TRANS (through) + LUC (light) = light passes through, but blurry.
examples: I felt my chin and found a translucent slick of sweat.
The bathroom window has translucent glass.

meaning: Across, from one side to the other
trick: TRANSVERSE = TRAVERSE across; -ALLY = in that way.
examples: The room was divided into three parts by high iron grilles running transversally.
Cut the carrot transversally into thin rounds.

meaning: Very dangerous, often in a hidden way; also not loyal, likely to betray
trick: TREACHEROUS waters 'TREAT' you nicely then CHEAT you.
examples: It's a place full of storms and treacherous waters.
The icy roads were treacherous this morning.

meaning: Put your foot down on something; walk on
trick: TREAD = to TREAD is to sTEP on a road.
examples: The hens and ducks were at pains not to tread on the chalk marks.
Please don't tread on the wet floor.

meaning: Formal written agreements between countries
trick: TREATIES = countries TREAT each other fairly on paper.
examples: People could handle everything from peace treaties to business mergers.
The two nations signed several trade treaties.

meaning: A long, serious written work on one subject
trick: A TREATISE TREATS a subject in detail.
examples: Getting to Yes was a groundbreaking treatise on negotiation.
He wrote a long treatise on Indian philosophy.

meaning: Small special things to eat or enjoy, like sweets
trick: TREATS are what you get when someone TREATS you nicely.
examples: After he was gone, Mariam would climb one of the willows with her treats.
Grandma always brings treats for the kids.

meaning: A formal written agreement between countries
trick: TREATY = countries agree to TREAT each other well.
examples: "They signed a treaty!" he said.
The two countries signed a peace treaty.

meaning: Having a frame or pattern of criss-crossed strips
trick: TRELLIS = criss-cross TRELLIS frame; TRELLISED = made like one.
examples: The cinema had private balcony seats and a trellised ceiling.
The garden had a trellised wall covered in roses.

meaning: Frames of criss-crossed wood or metal for climbing plants
trick: TRELLISES let plants TRAVEL upward like on a lattice ladder.
examples: In the garden, grape vines were clinging to wooden trellises.
We built wooden trellises for the tomato plants.

meaning: Very great in amount, size, or power
trick: TREMENDOUS makes the ground TREMBLE — that big.
examples: He was respected for his steadiness of character and tremendous powers of work.
She made a tremendous effort to finish on time.

meaning: A slight shaking of the ground (earthquake) or of the body
trick: TREMOR makes you TREMble.
examples: All we feel on the surface is a slight tremor.
We felt a small tremor during the night.

usage.pattern: a slight/small tremor / a tremor in someone's voice/hands

meaning: Shaking slightly, especially because of nervousness or excitement
trick: TREMULOUS = TREMbling voice, full of nerves.
examples: "She's agreed!" he said, his voice tremulous with excitement.
She gave a tremulous smile before her speech.

usage.pattern: a tremulous + voice/smile / tremulous with + feeling

meaning: A long narrow hole dug in the ground
trick: TRENCH = dig a long ditch like a TRENCH-coat soldier.
examples: My light was faint, and in the trench I couldn't see a thing.
Workers dug a trench for the water pipes.

usage.pattern: dig a trench / in a trench

meaning: In 'in the ...': doing the hard, practical, everyday work; also long narrow ditches
trick: Soldiers IN THE TRENCHES do the real dirty work.
examples: Sister Katherine toiled in the trenches with the same kid.
Nurses are the ones in the trenches during a crisis.

meaning: A person who enters a place or private area without permission
trick: TRESPASSER = PASSes into a space illegally.
examples: She was in his room for the first time, sitting on his bed, feeling like a trespasser.
The farmer chased the trespasser off his land.

usage.pattern: feel like a trespasser / trespassers on something

meaning: Frames with legs used to hold up a board as a table
trick: TRESTLES = legs that let a plank REST on them.
examples: The furniture consisted of some chairs and trestles.
They put boards on trestles to make a long table.

meaning: A difficult experience that tests someone; also the hearing of a case in court
trick: A TRIAL TRIes you — tests your strength.
examples: Behind every trial and every sorrow, God has a reason.
Losing his job was a real trial for him.

usage.pattern: a trial for someone / trials and troubles

meaning: Competitions held to choose the best people for a team or event; also tests
trick: TRIALS = you TRY out to get selected.
examples: These were the Olympic trials for negotiating.
She did well in the national swimming trials.

usage.pattern: the + Olympic/national trials / trials for something

meaning: A person who competes in races of swimming, cycling and running
trick: TRI (three) + ATHLETE = athlete of three sports.
examples: Being a triathlete had become an important part of Lindsay's identity.
My cousin trained for a year to become a triathlete.

meaning: Races made of swimming, cycling and running, one after another
trick: TRI (three) + ATHLON (contest) = three contests in one.
examples: SBG has raced triathlons and captained a team through the Eco-Challenge.
She has completed three triathlons this year.

meaning: Using clever tricks to fool people
trick: TRICKERY = full of TRICKs.
examples: Laila told her of his riddles, his trickery and mischief, his easy laugh.
The magician's show was all trickery.

meaning: Flowing slowly in a thin stream or small drops
trick: TRICKLING = a TRICKy little stream that barely flows.
examples: The squeals of girls and the trickling of bathwater echoed between the walls.
Water was trickling down the window.

meaning: The gold badge of a US Navy SEAL (shaped like a three-pointed spear); also a three-pointed spear
trick: TRI (three) + DENT (teeth) = three-toothed spear, like Shiva's trishul.
examples: My goal in SEAL training was more than making it through with a Trident.
Lord Shiva holds a trident in his hand.

meaning: The main kind of fat in the body and blood, used for energy
trick: TRI (three) + GLYCERIDES = three fatty chains on one glycerol.
examples: Some think it helps break down the glycogen and triglycerides muscles need.
The doctor checked my cholesterol and triglycerides.

meaning: A group of three books, films or plays on the same story
trick: TRI (three) + LOGY (stories) = three linked stories.
examples: Amish made Lord Shiva the hero of his trilogy.
I finished the whole trilogy in one week.

usage.pattern: a trilogy of + books/films / the final part of a trilogy

meaning: In 'in ...': three times over, or in three copies
trick: TRIPLICATE = TRIPLE copies; like DUPLICATE but three.
examples: When I teetered toward Kate I saw her in triplicate, six hands groping toward me.
Please submit the form in triplicate.

meaning: A great victory or success, or the joy felt from it; also a very successful piece of work
hindi: विजय, जीत की खुशी; बड़ी सफलता
trick: TRI-UMPH: TRY hard and you TRIUMPH.
examples: The animals chased the men down the track in triumph.
Winning the final was a moment of triumph for the team.

usage.pattern: in triumph / a shout of triumph / a triumph over something

meaning: Of little value or importance
trick: TRIVIAL = TRIVIA: small facts nobody really needs.
examples: We let trivial and hateful values take control of our desires.
Don't get angry over such a trivial matter.

meaning: Small, unimportant matters or details
trick: TRIVIALITIES = lots of TRIVIAL things.
examples: After the war they were unfazed by life's trivialities and petty annoyances.
Let's not waste time on trivialities and get to the main point.

usage.pattern: the trivialities of something / waste time on trivialities

meaning: Past tense of tread: walked or stepped; '... water' = kept upright in deep water by moving the legs
hindi: चला, कदम रखा; पानी में तैरता रहा
trick: TROD = TREAD in the past; TRODE-n't fall.
examples: She lay flat on the raft while I trod water.
He trod carefully on the icy path.

usage.pattern: tread (past: trod) on something / trod water

meaning: Past participle of tread: stepped or walked on, often crushed under feet
trick: TRODDEN = TROD + DEN: the den floor got TRODDEN flat.
examples: The ducklings looked for a place where they would not be trodden on.
The grass was trodden flat by the crowd.

usage.pattern: be trodden on / be trodden down

meaning: Walked together in a group, often in a line
hindi: झुंड में गए, एक साथ चले
trick: TROOPED like a TROOP of soldiers marching together.
examples: The animals trooped down to the hayfield to begin the harvest.
The children trooped into the classroom after lunch.

meaning: A soldier, especially in a cavalry or armoured unit; also (US) a state police officer
trick: A TROOPER is one member of a TROOP.
examples: It was some cheap, low-budget storm trooper.
My son dressed up as a storm trooper for the party.

meaning: Of or from the hot, wet parts of the world near the equator
trick: TROPICAL = from the TROPICS, where it is hot all year.
examples: The tropical heat was intense and sweat slid down my face.
We drank cold juice made from tropical fruit.

meaning: '... out' = repeated an old excuse or idea again; also ran at a slow, steady pace
trick: TROTTED OUT an old excuse, like a horse TROTTED round the ring again.
examples: Even in the SEALs I trotted out that lie.
The horse trotted slowly around the field.

usage.pattern: trot out something (an excuse/lie) / trot along/off

meaning: The foot of a pig
trick: A pig's TROTTER does the TROTTING.
examples: Major raised his trotter for silence.
The pig lifted one trotter out of the mud.

meaning: Running at a slow, steady pace, between walking and running
trick: TROT-TING: a slow TROT, like a pony.
examples: She did not turn to see him trotting alongside the bus.
The little dog came trotting after me.

meaning: A long, narrow open container for animals' food or water; also a low point
trick: TROUGH sounds like TROFF: the pigs scoff from the TROUGH.
examples: He brought a few sheep and built them a feeding trough.
The horses drank water from the trough.

meaning: A piece of clothing covering each leg separately, from the waist to the ankles
trick: TROUSERS: TWO-SERS, two legs in one piece.
examples: He was wearing blue trousers, a white shirt, and a straw hat.
I need a new pair of trousers for the office.

usage.pattern: a pair of trousers / wear trousers

meaning: A fish of rivers and lakes, often caught for food
trick: TROUT gets caught OUT of the river.
examples: He showed her how to cast her line and reel in the trout.
We had grilled trout for dinner by the lake.

usage.pattern: catch a trout / fish for trout

meaning: Walked slowly with heavy steps because tired or unhappy
trick: TRUDGED through the SLUDGE: slow, heavy steps.
examples: She trudged home, hurt and sad, without seeing Aziza.
We trudged through the snow to the bus stop.

meaning: Invented or exaggerated, not true; also (of charges) falsely made up
trick: TRUMPED-UP: blown up like a TRUMPET, all noise and no truth.
examples: Her low voice made Laila's promises sound trumped-up and foolish.
He was arrested on trumped-up charges.

meaning: A brass musical instrument you blow into, making a loud bright sound
trick: TRUM-PET: TRUMP-et blows his own TRUMPET loudly.
examples: I heard the tin trumpet of an ice-cream seller in the street.
My brother is learning to play the trumpet.

usage.pattern: play the trumpet / blow a trumpet

meaning: Someone who plays the trumpet; here, someone who announces another's arrival loudly
trick: TRUMPETER = TRUMPET + ER: the one who blows it.
examples: A black cockerel marched in front of him and acted as a kind of trumpeter.
The trumpeter played a loud note to open the parade.

usage.pattern: act as a trumpeter / a + adjective + trumpeter

meaning: Tests where people show their skill to be chosen for a team or part
trick: TRYOUTS: you TRY OUT for the team.
examples: When tryouts started, I handled the ball a lot.
She practised every day before the basketball tryouts.

usage.pattern: tryouts for something / go to tryouts

meaning: Secret, romantic meetings between lovers
trick: TRYSTS: they TRY to keep their meetings a SECRET.
examples: I have found this more rewarding than any of the flings and trysts I had in the past.
The two lovers had secret trysts in the old garden.

usage.pattern: a tryst with someone / secret trysts

meaning: A plant with strongly scented white flowers
trick: TUBEROSE: a ROSE-like flower growing from a TUBER (bulb).
examples: He chose the name because Mariam, the tuberose, was a lovely flower.
The room smelled sweet from the vase of tuberoses.

meaning: A small bunch of hair, grass or feathers growing close together
trick: TUFT: a TUFT of hair is a little TUFTY bunch.
examples: She looked at the baby, the tuft of dark hair, the hazel eyes, the pink cheeks.
A tuft of grass grew between the stones.

meaning: Pulling hard or suddenly
trick: TUG-boats are TUGGING ships into the harbour.
examples: There was patting, clutching and tugging as the children climbed into her arms.
The child kept tugging at his mother's sleeve.

meaning: Brightly coloured, cup-shaped spring flowers that grow from bulbs
trick: TULIPS look like red LIPS (TU-LIPS).
examples: Their lips were red as tulips.
Red and yellow tulips bloomed in the park.

usage.pattern: a bunch of tulips / plant tulips

meaning: Fell suddenly and rolled over; also messy and untidy
trick: TUMBLED like a TUMBLER (acrobat) rolling over.
examples: I needed to notice when my body was failing, long before I tumbled into that trap.
The boy tripped and tumbled down the stairs.

meaning: Falling quickly while rolling over and over
trick: TUMBLING like clothes in a TUMBLE dryer.
examples: Standing at the cliff edge, I kept picturing tripping and tumbling down.
The apples came tumbling out of the bag.

usage.pattern: come tumbling down/out / tumbling down something

meaning: Very loud, confused or full of upheaval
trick: TUMULTUOUS = full of TUMULT (noise and chaos).
examples: It's a tumultuous place, full of storms and dangerous waters.
They went through a tumultuous year after moving cities.

meaning: Loose pieces of clothing that cover the body down to the hips or knees
trick: TUNICS: TUNE-ICS, dancers in long TUNICS.
examples: People in bright tunics were laying out the harvest to dry on the roofs.
The students wore white tunics for the school play.

meaning: A long cloth wound round the head, worn especially by Sikh and some Muslim men
trick: TURBAN: TURN-BAND, a band you TURN round your head.
examples: The shadow of his turban fell on a patch of buttercups.
My grandfather wears a white turban every day.

usage.pattern: wear a turban / tie a turban

meaning: Emotional or social disorder and instability; also rough, uneven air movement
trick: TURBULENCE: like a TURBINE spinning wildly.
examples: You must accept the emotional turbulence that comes with facing rejections.
The plane shook as we flew through some turbulence.

meaning: Rude slang: a lump of solid waste from an animal or person; also an offensive word for a nasty person
trick: TURD: a cow's TURD lies in the field like a TURF clump. (Rude word.)
examples: Grandpa said, Gee whiz, I sure do feel like a cow turd today.
He stepped on a dog turd on the pavement.

meaning: A state of great worry, confusion or disorder
trick: TURMOIL: TURN and BOIL inside, all mixed up.
examples: When I was all alone in Carmel, I was in turmoil.
The country was in turmoil after the election.

usage.pattern: be in turmoil / throw something into turmoil

meaning: A round white root vegetable, eaten cooked
trick: TURNIP: TURN it UP from the soil, a round root.
examples: She learned to cook stew with turnip and spinach sabzi.
My mother added turnip to the soup.

meaning: Farm machines for cutting turnips into pieces for animal feed
trick: TURNIP-SLICERS: they SLICE TURNIPS for the cattle.
examples: His imagination had run far beyond chaff-cutters and turnip-slicers.
The farmer bought two new turnip-slicers for the winter feed.

meaning: A bright greenish-blue colour; also a blue-green gemstone
trick: TURQUOISE: TURKISH stone, the colour of the sea near Turkey.
examples: She had inherited her thick-lashed, turquoise green eyes.
She wore a turquoise dress to the wedding.

meaning: Old word: long pointed teeth (tusks) of an animal such as a boar
trick: TUSHES = TUSKS with a soft SH.
examples: He was still a majestic pig, though his tushes had never been cut.
The wild boar showed its sharp tushes.

meaning: A small tool with two thin arms for picking up or pulling out tiny things
trick: TWEEZERS: SQUEEZE the TWEEZERS to pull a hair.
examples: She had plucked Giti's chin hair with tweezers.
I used tweezers to take the splinter out of my finger.

usage.pattern: a pair of tweezers / pluck something with tweezers

meaning: Twisted or turned something with the fingers, often without thinking
trick: TWIDDLED: TWIRLED + FIDDLED.
examples: Mariam twiddled a strand of Laila's hair.
He twiddled the knob on the radio.

meaning: Twisting or turning something with the fingers, often from nerves or boredom
trick: TWIDDLING thumbs = bored FIDDLING.
examples: He began twiddling his white mustache.
Stop twiddling your thumbs and help me.

meaning: A small thin branch of a tree or bush
trick: TWIG: a TWIG is a TINY branch.
examples: She would make them out of pieces of twig and decorate them with a flower.
The bird carried a twig to its nest.

usage.pattern: a twig of + plant / snap a twig

meaning: Small thin branches of a tree or bush
trick: TWIGS: TWIG + S, a bundle of tiny branches.
examples: Kissing his hand felt like kissing a set of twigs covered with thin skin.
We gathered dry twigs to start the fire.

meaning: Gave a sudden short sharp pain
trick: TWINGED: a TWIN pair of sharp pains, then gone.
examples: Each time my tendon twinged, it felt like a raw nerve.
My knee twinged as I climbed the stairs.

meaning: Twisting or winding around something
trick: TWINING like TWINE (string) wrapped round and round.
examples: The ivy was twining round the old fence.
Her fingers were twining a ribbon round a pencil.

meaning: Shining with a gentle flickering light
trick: TWINKLE TWINKLE little star: TWINKLING stars.
examples: Bees were buzzing over twinkling wildflowers.
We lay on the grass watching the twinkling stars.

usage.pattern: twinkling + noun / in the twinkling of an eye

meaning: A quick spin round; here '... dress' = a dress that flares out when you spin
trick: TWIRL like a GIRL spinning in a party dress.
examples: There was a twirl dress with little pink fishes sewn around it.
She did a twirl to show off her new skirt.

usage.pattern: do a twirl / twirl something / twirl around

meaning: Turned or spun something round and round quickly
trick: TWIRLED: a GIRL TWIRLED her hair.
examples: Mullah Faizullah twirled the beads of his rosary as they walked.
She twirled around in her new dress.

meaning: Turning something round and round quickly
trick: TWIRLING: TWIST + WHIRLING.
examples: Jalil kept twirling his wedding band with a helpless look.
The dancer was twirling across the stage.

meaning: To make a small sudden movement you don't control
trick: TWITCH: a little ITCH that makes you jerk.
examples: I didn't even twitch, and I saw how much that bothered him.
His eye began to twitch when he was tired.

meaning: A very strong tropical storm with violent winds, especially in the western Pacific
trick: TYPHOON: TIE-FOON, a storm that ties ships in knots.
examples: More pain swirled within me like a typhoon.
The typhoon closed schools across the city.

usage.pattern: a typhoon hits somewhere / like a typhoon

meaning: Using power in a cruel, unfair and controlling way
trick: TYRANNICAL = acting like a TYRANT.
examples: If they went hungry, it was not from feeding tyrannical human beings.
The workers hated their tyrannical boss.

meaning: British spelling: to rule over or treat someone cruelly and unfairly
trick: TYRANNISE = behave like a TYRANT.
examples: No animal must ever tyrannise over his own kind.
The older boys used to tyrannise the younger ones.

meaning: Cruel and unfair use of power or control; also something that controls you harshly
trick: TYRANNY: what a TYRANT runs.
examples: All the evils of this life spring from the tyranny of human beings.
The people rose up against tyranny.

usage.pattern: the tyranny of someone/something / fight tyranny

meaning: A ruler or person who uses power cruelly and unfairly
trick: TYRANT: TIRE-ANT, a ruler who tires out his people.
examples: Soon or late, Tyrant Man shall be overthrown.
The old king was a cruel tyrant.

usage.pattern: a cruel tyrant / overthrow a tyrant
